title: Three implementations of a lexicographic objective

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A MathOpt model minimizes cost as its primary objective (priority 0) and maximizes service level as an auxiliary objective (priority 1). A colleague ports it with setObjectiveN(cost, index=0, priority=0, weight=-1) and setObjectiveN(service, index=1, priority=1) under ModelSense maximize. What does Gurobi optimize first?

options.text: Cost, since index 0 is always the primary objective in either API
options.says: The index names the objective; the order of passes comes from the priorities alone.

options.text: Cost, since the lowest priority number is optimized first in either API
options.says: Lowest first is MathOpt's rule; Gurobi runs the passes in decreasing priority.

options.text: Service, since Gurobi optimizes the highest priority number first
options.says: Right: copied unchanged, MathOpt's numbers reverse the order in Gurobi.

options.text: Both at once, since every objective in one ModelSense is blended
options.says: Only objectives with equal priority are blended; these two have different priorities.

origin.section: gurobipy Solves the Hierarchy Natively, and Its Priorities Run the Other Way

questions.stem: A model in the course's runner holds NPV as its primary objective and two auxiliary objectives, with a tolerance on NPV. How do you get its plan there?

options.text: Send it to HiGHS, which reads each objective and tolerance in priority order
options.says: HiGHS refuses the model: 'Highs does not support multiple objectives'.

options.text: Solve one objective at a time, each kept within its tolerance
options.says: Right: solve_in_order or the manual passes run on any MIP solver, and matched setObjectiveN.

options.text: Send it to Gurobi through MathOpt, which takes every objective
options.says: In OR-Tools 9.15 MathOpt cannot load the runner's Gurobi 13 library, so that solve never runs.

options.text: Send it to CP-SAT, which accepts any number of objectives
options.says: CP-SAT refuses the model too, as lesson 4.3.2 showed.

origin.section: MathOpt Stores the Hierarchy in the Model, and Every Runner Solver Refuses It

questions.stem: A manual two-pass solve keeps NPV with no tolerance, but pass 1 stops at a 3% gap and the kept row uses the plan pass 1 returned. What can pass 2 do?

options.text: Give up NPV that no tolerance allowed, since the row sits at the early plan
options.says: Right: at a 5% gap HiGHS kept NPV above $24,071k, and pass 2 gave up $162k of NPV.

options.text: Nothing different, since a kept row with no tolerance holds NPV at its optimum
options.says: The row holds NPV at the plan pass 1 returned, which can lie below the optimum.

options.text: Fail every time, since a row built from an early plan is always infeasible
options.says: A row built from pass 1's own plan is met by that plan, so pass 2 always has a feasible plan.

options.text: Return the same plan as at a zero gap, since pass 2 itself is solved to a zero gap
options.says: Pass 2 works above a lower floor; at a 5% gap in pass 1 the final plan changed (NPV $24,098k, not $24,260k).

origin.section: Solve Each Pass to a Zero Gap, or the Gap Becomes a Tolerance

concepts: what a gap left in the first pass does to the second
the order of passes after a port from MathOpt to gurobipy
